ಏರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def make_problems(r, tier, n):
    lo, hi = TIERS[tier]
    return [(r.randint(lo, hi), r.randint(lo, hi)) for _ in range(n)]


def generate(r, comp, tier, a, b):
    """Returns (answer, good_reasoning). A wrong path still lands on the right answer one time in three (offset 0 is 2 of the 6 choices), which is the shortcut."""
    if r.random() < comp[tier]:
        return a + b, True
    off = r.choice([-2, -1, 0, 0, 1, 2])
    return a + b + off, False


def rationalize(r, tier, a, b, hint_success=0.6):
    """Given the correct answer as a hint, the model writes a rationale that reaches it; assumed to be good reasoning only some of the time."""
    return (r.random() < hint_success)


def star_round(r, comp, n, use_rationalization, lr=0.6):
    stats = {}
    for tier in TIERS:
        probs = make_problems(r, tier, n)
        kept_good = kept_short = rat_good = 0
        for a, b in probs:
            ans, good = generate(r, comp, tier, a, b)
            if ans == a + b:
                if good:
                    kept_good += 1
                else:
                    kept_short += 1
            elif use_rationalization and rationalize(r, tier, a, b):
                rat_good += 1
        stats[tier] = (kept_good, kept_short, rat_good)
    for tier, (g, s, rg) in stats.items():
        rate = (g + rg) / n
        comp[tier] = min(0.99, comp[tier] + lr * rate * (1 - comp[tier]))
    return stats


def accuracy(r, comp, tier, n=400):
    probs = make_problems(r, tier, n)
    return mean(generate(r, comp, tier, a, b)[0] == a + b for a, b in probs)"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"st_1.py","headingEn":"main(): experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() shows what the filter keeps, runs five rounds with and without rationalization, repeats over ten seeds and reports the shortcut share of the kept data.","descKn":"main() ಶೋಧಕ ಏನು ಇಡುತ್ತದೆ ತೋರಿಸಿ, rationalization ಇಲ್ಲದೆ ಮತ್ತು ಇರುವಂತೆ ಐದು ಸುತ್ತು ಓಡಿಸಿ, ಹತ್ತು seeds ಮೇಲೆ ಪುನರಾವರ್ತಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಇಟ್ಟ ದತ್ತಾಂಶದ ಶಾರ್ಟ್‌ಕಟ್ ಪಾಲು ವರದಿ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():

        print(f"{tier:6} competence {comp[tier]:.2f}: kept {g + s:3d} of 200 | genuine {g:3d} | shortcut {s:3d}")
    print("the filter keeps every rationale whose final answer is right, including wrong-path rationales that landed on the right answer by luck, so the kept set is a little contaminated and the hard tier gives the least training data; competence values are invented starting points")

    """Returns (answer, good_reasoning). A wrong path still lands on the right answer one time in three (offset 0 is 2 of the 6 choices), which is the shortcut."""
    if r.random() < comp[tier]:
        return a + b, True
    off = r.choice([-2, -1, 0, 0, 1, 2])
    return a + b + off, False


def rationalize(r, tier, a, b, hint_success=0.6):
    """Given the correct answer as a hint, the model writes a rationale that reaches it; assumed to be good reasoning only some of the time."""
    return (r.random() < hint_success)


def star_round(r, comp, n, use_rationalization, lr=0.6):
    stats = {}

    """n candidate answers; each is the right answer 0 with probability p, else one of wrong_pool wrong answers (1..wrong_pool)."""
    return [0 if r.random() < p else r.randint(1, wrong_pool) for _ in range(n)]


def pick_random(r, c):
    return r.choice(c)


def pick_majority(r, c):
    cnt = Counter(c)
    top = max(cnt.values())
    return r.choice([k for k, v in cnt.items() if v == top])


def pick_verified(r, c, tpr, fpr):
    """Verifier accepts a right candidate with probability tpr and a wrong one with probability fpr; pick randomly among accepted, else fall back to random."""
    accepted = [x for x in c if r.random() < (tpr if x == 0 else fpr)]
    return r.choice(accepted) if accepted else r.choice(c)


def rate(fn, p, n, trials, seed, **kw):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    return mean(fn(r, candidates(r, p, n), **kw) == 0 for _ in range(trials))"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"st_2.py","headingEn":"main(): experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() compares the rules with the formula, varies verifier error rates, adds correlated failures and trains a threshold verifier.","descKn":"main() ನಿಯಮಗಳನ್ನು ಸೂತ್ರದೊಂದಿಗೆ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, ಪರಿಶೀಲಕ ದೋಷ ದರ ಬದಲಿಸಿ, ಸಹಸಂಬಂಧಿತ ವೈಫಲ್ಯ ಸೇರಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಮಿತಿ ಪರಿಶೀಲಕಕ್ಕೆ ತರಬೇತಿ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    T = 20000
    section("1. Genuinely measuring: random pick, majority vote and a perfect checker against the formula (p = 0.3)")
    for n in (1, 4, 16):
        ideal = 1 - (1 - 0.3) ** n
        rnd = rate(pick_random, 0.3, n, T, 1)
        maj = rate(pick_majority, 0.3, n, T, 1)
        ver = rate(pick_verified, 0.3, n, T, 1, tpr=1.0, fpr=0.0)
        print(f"N={n:2d}: formula {ideal:.3f} | perfect verifier {ver:.3f} | majority {maj:.3f} | random {rnd:.3f}")
    print("a perfect checker matches 1 - (1 - p)^N, random choice never improves on p, and majority vote helps here only because wrong answers are spread over seven values while the right one is a single value; if wrong answers agreed with each other majority vote would fail")

    section("2. Genuinely measuring: verifier errors cap the gain (p = 0.3, N = 16)")
    for tpr, fpr in ((1.0, 0.0), (0.9, 0.1), (0.9, 0.3), (0.7, 0.3), (0.5, 0.5)):
        v = rate(pick_verified, 0.3, 16, T, 2, tpr=tpr, fpr=fpr)
        print(f"verifier true-positive {tpr:.1f}, false-positive {fpr:.1f}: success {v:.3f}")
    print("success falls as the false-positive rate rises and equals the base rate 0.300 when the verifier accepts right and wrong answers equally often, so a weak verifier can make extra samples worthless; the rates are invented")

    section("3. Genuinely measuring: when failures are correlated, more samples help less (N = 16)")
    r = random.Random(4)
    hits = 0
    for _ in range(T):
        hard = r.random() < 0.5
        p = 0.02 if hard else 0.58
        c = candidates(r, p, 16)
        hits += pick_verified(r, c, 1.0, 0.0) == 0
    print(f"average p is 0.30 but half the problems are hard (0.02) and half easy (0.58): perfect-verifier success {hits / T:.3f} against the independent formula {1 - 0.7 ** 16:.3f}")
    print("a perfect verifier cannot select an answer that was never sampled, so the gain is bounded by how often the right answer appears at all; the 0.02 and 0.58 split is invented")

    section("4. Genuinely running: training a verifier on both correct and incorrect samples")
    r = random.Random(7)
    data = []
    for _ in range(4000):
        correct = r.random() < 0.3
        score = r.gauss(1.0 if correct else 0.0, 1.0)
        data.append((score, correct))
    best_t, best_acc = None, 0
    for t in [x / 10 for x in range(-10, 21)]:
        acc = mean((s > t) == c for s, c in data)
        if acc > best_acc:
            best_t, best_acc = t, acc
    test = []
    for _ in range(4000):
        correct = r.random() < 0.3
        test.append((r.gauss(1.0 if correct else 0.0, 1.0), correct))
    tacc = mean((s > best_t) == c for s, c in test)
    tpr = mean(s > best_t for s, c in test if c)
    fpr = mean(s > best_t for s, c in test if not c)
    print(f"threshold {best_t} chosen on training data | held-out accuracy {tacc:.3f} | true-positive {tpr:.3f} | false-positive {fpr:.3f}")
    print("the scripted scores overlap, so the threshold that maximises accuracy on this 30 percent correct mix rejects most right answers (low true-positive rate) in order to keep false positives low; V-STaR trains a verifier on the model's own wrong samples as well as right ones to learn that boundary, but a real verifier is a trained model and this one is a threshold on invented Gaussian scores")

outcome_reward ಮತ್ತು process_reward ಅದಕ್ಕೆ ಎರಡು ವಿಭಿನ್ನ ರೀತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುತ್ತವೆ.","code":"def make_chain(r, n_steps=4, p_step=0.8, lucky=0.2):
    """A reasoning chain: each step is right with p_step. If any step is wrong the final answer is still right with probability lucky."""
    steps = [r.random() < p_step for _ in range(n_steps)]
    if all(steps):
        return steps, True
    return steps, r.random() < lucky


def outcome_reward(chain):
    return 1.0 if chain[1] else 0.0


def process_reward(chain):
    return mean(chain[0])"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"st_3.py","headingEn":"main(): experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() measures outcome rewards, compares the two filters, degrades the step checker, tests a memorizer and an algorithm out of distribution and tries thinking gates.","descKn":"main() outcome ಬಹುಮಾನ ಅಳೆದು, ಎರಡು ಶೋಧಕ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, ಹಂತ ಪರಿಶೀಲಕ ಹದಗೆಡಿಸಿ, ವಿತರಣೆ-ಹೊರಗೆ memorizer ಮತ್ತು algorithm ಪರೀಕ್ಷಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಯೋಚನೆ ಗೇಟ್ ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely measuring: what outcome rewards reward (20000 chains of 4 steps, per-step 0.8)")
    r = random.Random(1)
    chains = [make_chain(r) for _ in range(20000)]
    right = [c for c in chains if c[1]]
    clean = [c for c in right if all(c[0])]
    print(f"answer right: {len(right) / len(chains):.3f} | all steps right: {sum(all(c[0]) for c in chains) / len(chains):.3f}")
    print(f"of the chains an outcome reward scores 1.0, the share with at least one wrong step: {1 - len(clean) / len(right):.3f}")
    print("an outcome-only reward treats a chain with wrong steps and a lucky right answer exactly like a clean chain, so a notable share of rewarded chains reasoned badly; the 0.8 per-step rate and 20 percent luck are invented")

    section("2. Genuinely measuring: filtering by outcome against filtering by process")
    keep_out = [c for c in chains if outcome_reward(c) == 1.0]
    keep_proc = [c for c in chains if process_reward(c) == 1.0]
    print(f"outcome filter keeps {len(keep_out)} chains; fraction fully correct {mean(all(c[0]) for c in keep_out):.3f}")
    print(f"process filter keeps {len(keep_proc)} chains; fraction fully correct {mean(all(c[0]) for c in keep_proc):.3f}")
    print("requiring every step to be checked removes the lucky chains and keeps fewer examples, which is the trade of process supervision: cleaner data at the price of needing a per-step checker, and here the checker is perfect because the lab knows the truth")

    section("3. Genuinely measuring: an imperfect step checker")
    r = random.Random(2)
    for miss in (0.0, 0.1, 0.3):
        kept = []
        for steps, ans in chains[:8000]:
            flagged = any((not s) and r.random() >= miss for s in steps)
            if not flagged:
                kept.append((steps, ans))
        print(f"checker misses {miss:.1f} of wrong steps: kept {len(kept):4d} | fully correct share {mean(all(s) for s, _ in kept):.3f}")
    print("as the checker misses more wrong steps, bad chains slip into the training set again; a process checker is only as good as its coverage, and the miss rates are invented")

    section("4. Genuinely running: a memorizer and an algorithm, tested in and out of distribution")
    train = {(a, b): a + b for a in range(10, 100, 3) for b in range(10, 100, 3)}
    memorizer = lambda a, b: train.get((a, b), 0)
    algorithm = lambda a, b: a + b
    r = random.Random(3)
    in_dist = [(r.choice(range(10, 100, 3)), r.choice(range(10, 100, 3))) for _ in range(500)]
    unseen = [(a + 1, b + 1) for a, b in in_dist]
    big = [(r.randint(1000, 9999), r.randint(1000, 9999)) for _ in range(500)]
    for name, f in (("memorizer", memorizer), ("algorithm", algorithm)):
        acc = [mean(f(a, b) == a + b for a, b in s) for s in (in_dist, unseen, big)]
        print(f"{name:10} in-distribution {acc[0]:.2f} | unseen two-digit {acc[1]:.2f} | four-digit {acc[2]:.2f}")
    print("both look perfect on training-style inputs, and only the one that learned the procedure survives inputs it has not seen; a test set drawn from the training distribution cannot tell them apart, and the memorizer is a plain lookup table used as a stand-in")

    section("5. Genuinely measuring: a thinking gate that thinks only when a position looks hard")
    r = random.Random(4)
    positions = [r.random() for _ in range(20000)]
    accuracy = lambda d, think: 0.97 if think else max(0.2, 1.0 - 0.9 * d)
    for name, gate in (("never think", lambda d: False), ("always think", lambda d: True), ("think if difficulty > 0.5", lambda d: d > 0.5), ("think if difficulty > 0.8", lambda d: d > 0.8)):
        thought = [gate(d) for d in positions]
        acc = mean(accuracy(d, t) for d, t in zip(positions, thought))
        print(f"{name:27} accuracy {acc:.3f} | thinking tokens per position {mean(thought) * 50:5.1f}")
    print("thinking only where difficulty exceeds 0.5 recovers about 76 percent of the accuracy gain of always thinking (0.556 to 0.870 against 0.970) for about half the tokens, because thinking only helps where the position is hard; the difficulty scores and the accuracy curve are invented, and a real model has to learn when to think")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"
